claim_audit_results.claim_summary: Objectives pertinent to MSCA-PF 2026 call, addressing scientific gaps and researcher skill development sought by expected outcomes.
Selected call is HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01.
European Postdoctoral Fellowship with 6-month non-academic placement extension.
30-month duration (24-month host phase plus 6-month placement).
Host is HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (ATK), Martonvásár, Hungary.
Experienced researcher is Dr. Rositsa Cholakova.
Primary supervisor at HUN-REN ATK is Prof. Tibor Janda.
Programme organised around four objectives O1-O4 with verbatim canonical titles.
Central challenge: whether a tomato water-stress signal stays biologically meaningful across seasons/scales, survives field validation, and is encoded in a crop-configurable DSS.
Objectives close three gaps: physiological grounding, transferability, irrigation decision relevance.
Each objective defined by concrete measurable outputs.
Objectives anchored to dated deliverables (D1.1/D1.2/D2.2 m14, D2.1 m3, D3.1/D3.2 m18, D4.1 m24, D5.1/D5.2 m30).
Pre-registered metrics under blocked unseen-year validation, thresholds fixed in D1.2, model frozen before first field season.
O1/O2 grounded in 2022-2026 MATE processing-tomato archive.
DrR is the fellow's pre-existing self-financed tool used as research-to-application vehicle.
O3 validated at an independent commercial farmer site instrumented by the project, with contingency ladder.
O4 relies on Krumatic software development and AgroVIR consultation plus M25-M30 evaluation/placement.
Extension to further crops/Bulgarian conditions is a post-MSCA route via MVCRI, no in-action MVCRI effort.
Ambition expressed as seven concrete transitions beyond the state of the art.
Project explicitly refuses four common assumptions.
Novelty is a physiologically grounded validation framework; parsimony/interpretability, no deep-learning dependency.
Framework separates reusable core from crop-specific components with crop-transfer gates.
Methodology reuses existing 2022-2026 archive harmonised into a QC-controlled matrix (O1).
Physiologically meaningful stress target fixed before modelling, replacing spectral proxies.
Predictive framework parsimonious/interpretable/uncertainty-aware, avoiding deep learning.
Four testable hypotheses H1-H4 underpin the work.
Model learns operational predictors vs an independent physiological stress target.
Model selection/evaluation use blocked, leakage-safe unseen-year temporal validation.
Pre-registered metrics with literature-derived thresholds fixed before the prospective season.
Primary model frozen and model card registered (D2.1, m3) before first field season.
Transferability treated at three levels: temporal, environmental, methodological/crop.
Frozen model validated prospectively at an instrumented commercial field, with limited-recalibration protocol (O3).
Reusable decision-support core separated from crop-specific parameters with recalibration gates.

DrR used as research-to-application vehicle; only validated components incorporated; software follows the science.
Archive heterogeneity/missingness mitigated by common-variable matrix and defined statistical unit.
UAV/hyperspectral fragility mitigated by prioritising acquisitions and retaining physiology/proximal core pathway.
Interdisciplinary integration of physiology, data science, EO and software/FMIS is necessary and structured.
Physiology strand anchored in HUN-REN ATK Plant Physiology and Metabolomics Dept; modelling under HUN-REN supervision.
Krumatic provides software development from start; AgroVIR provides requirements consultation and later evaluation.
